editorial: This report includes the trends that emerged today for the first time, without repeating what we have shared in recent days.

items.title: basecamp/omarchy
items.summary: Developed by Basecamp, Omarchy is a modern and original configuration tool for Linux operating systems. It offers a shell script-based approach to standardize system installations and facilitate management.

items.title: Firefox for iOS now has a native adblocker
items.summary: Mozilla added a built-in ad blocker feature to the Firefox internet browser it developed for iOS. This update allows users to block ads and trackers on web pages directly from the browser without the need for a third-party plug-in.

items.title: Claude: System Prompts
items.summary: Anthropic has made the system prompts feature available to developers for its artificial intelligence model Claude. This feature allows developers to manage the model's behavior, tone, and constraints with predefined instructions.

items.title: A 3rd World Embedded Engineer Responds to "RISC-V They Should Have Known Better"
items.summary: Embedded systems engineers in developing countries state that the low-cost and open-source nature of RISC-V architecture offers a critical opportunity for local technology ecosystems. This architecture enables independent development by democratizing hardware design processes that are inaccessible due to licensing fees.

items.title: Tell HN: Cloudflare silently injects its analytics when you switch nameservers
items.summary: Internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare automatically adds analytics snippets to websites if users move their name servers to its own system. This causes tracking scripts to be included even in static pages that do not contain any JavaScript code.

items.title: The AI Credit Resale Economy
items.summary: An economy is emerging where API credits that provide access to artificial intelligence models are resold at discounted prices in secondary markets. Token brokers acquire large-scale usage rights at low cost and market these tokens to smaller developers or businesses.

items.title: PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5: A Toolkit for Robot Process Assessment
items.summary: PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5 is a toolkit that evaluates the performance of robotic models with detailed process metrics beyond binary success rates. It analyzes the operations performed by robots through video recordings and provides concrete data on issues such as margin of error, recovery process and application quality.

items.title: MobileMem: Learning from a Year of Mobile Experiences
items.summary: MobileMem offers a new framework that enables artificial intelligence assistants to continuously learn by keeping user experiences in long-term memory. It aims to enable assistants to have a memory structure that develops over time by processing complex, multimodal and personal data on mobile devices.

items.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
items.summary: Developed to parse internal features in multimodal large language models, MMDiff enables to identify components that change during the training process of the model. This method enables inspection and targeted control of complex visual-textual structures using sparse autoencoders.

items.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing
items.summary: CPI-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark tool developed to evaluate visual editing models in real-world scenarios. Unlike existing tests, it aims to analyze the performance of models with more realistic criteria in complex and multi-image tasks.

items.title: Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction
items.summary: GAS improves the performance of multimodal large language models with a training method that combines visual comprehension and production. The method enables more effective processing of visual data by using decoupled embedding prediction without increasing the inference cost.

items.title: I thought I was building a C replacement. I was wrong
items.summary: Although the C3 programming language was developed to eliminate the shortcomings of the C language, it is a system language that has evolved into its own unique structure over time. Developers note that it is more efficient to design a new language (C3) that focuses on modern software needs rather than modifying an existing language.

items.title: Every Fucking Website
items.summary: Interface elements such as cookie consents, newsletter sign-up windows and notification requests that hide the content of modern websites turn into a mess that negatively affects the user experience. This situation increases criticism against the spread of dark patterns that make it difficult to access information on the internet.

items.title: A faster way to calculate the day-of-the-week
items.summary: The new algorithm developed by Ben Joffe offers a mathematical shortcut to calculate which day of the week any date falls on. This method provides fast results with fewer processing steps compared to traditional calendar calculations (Zeller formula).
